foodNote: Typical values for a home kitchen, for the portion named next to each number. Other sites often show bigger numbers because they count a bigger serving or a restaurant recipe. Your own katori, roti and oil change the number; Slate adjusts for them.

hub.title: Calories in Indian food: roti, dal, rice and more
hub.description: Calories, protein, carbs and fat for everyday Indian dishes, by katori, piece and plate, worked out from IFCT 2017 recipes in grams.
intro: Calories, protein, carbs and fat for everyday Indian food, in the portions you actually eat: a roti, a katori, a plate, a cup.
Every number is worked out from a recipe in grams and the Indian Food Composition Tables (IFCT 2017). Each page shows the recipe, the arithmetic and the sources.
